title: MCP: a banned person's AI assistant is still recorded as used, because the last-use stamp (#30918) runs before the ban refusal
body:
domain:server#1 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cytLmJxfAmgPVjUbbW

Filing gate: ① a named location, from the contract review of PR #30946 (card #30918, record 6686013581), should-fix item 5; the dev noted it in the report on #30918 and did not file it. ⛔ Not a claim.

PR #30946 adds `sys_oauth_consent.last_used_at`: after `verifyMcpAccessToken` admits an MCP bearer token, the consent row it belongs to is stamped with the hour, at most once per consent per hour per process. The card's rule 6 says the time is recorded only on a verified MCP call.

The MCP door reads the ban after the verifier: `packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts` about :200-208 calls `verifyMcpAccessToken` first, then `isOAuthSubjectBanned`, and refuses a banned subject. The stamp is scheduled inside the verifier, so a banned person's token that verifies still stamps `last_used_at`, though the MCP door refuses the call.

Reach: an administrator reading `GET /admin/authorized-clients?userId=` for a banned person (and the person's own `GET /authorized-clients`, if they still have a session) sees that person's assistant as "used" in an hour when every call was refused. Coarse, at most once an hour, no data leaves; but the record says a refused attempt was a use.

Wanted: the stamp records only a call the MCP door admitted, a banned subject's included. Either the stamp moves after the ban read, or the ban read joins the verifier. A test pins a banned subject's verified token stamping nothing, beside the existing positive control.

Suggested grade: p3, `domain:server`. Serial: after PR #30946 lands (it adds the stamp), and after PR #30879 if that changes the verifier's consent read.
